title: How Much Fiber in Broccoli? 5.1g per Cup
description: Broccoli: about 5.1 g of fiber per 1 cup chopped, cooked (18% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in broccoli?

answer.detail: fiber in 1 cup chopped, cooked (156 g)
answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Broccoli, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

intro: Broccoli ranks #3 of 10 vegetables on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in broccoli by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in broccoli?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists broccoli, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt at 3.3 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup chopped, cooked; 156 g) therefore has about 5.1 g of fiber and 55 calories. That is 18% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 21% of a 25 g day and 14% of a 38 g day.
Broccoli is the vegetable most people think of for fiber. A cup of cooked broccoli gives a solid few grams, and because it is so low in calories, it ranks high on fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Raw vs cooked broccoli
paragraphs: Cooking does not create fiber, but it shrinks broccoli, so a cooked cup holds more broccoli than a raw cup. That is why the cooked cup in the table has about twice the fiber of the raw cup.
An older version of USDA’s data paired “1 cup” with a half-cup weight, which made cooked broccoli look lower than it is. This site uses the corrected 156 g cup.

sections.heading: How broccoli compares with other vegetables
paragraphs: Of the 10 vegetables on this site, broccoli ranks #3 for fiber per typical serving and #4 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 9.4 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [kale](/fiber-in-kale) at 4.7 g (1 cup, cooked); [spinach](/fiber-in-spinach) at 4.3 g (1 cup, cooked); [Brussels sprouts](/fiber-in-brussels-sprouts) at 4.1 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), broccoli is #7 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding broccoli to your day
paragraphs: Roast a sheet pan of broccoli for the week, or add a cup of florets to pasta, stir-fries, and grain bowls.

Example: 1 cup broccoli, 1 cup brown rice, 1/2 cup edamame. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 12.3 g of fiber, with 5.1 g from the broccoli. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of broccoli?
faqs.a: 3.3 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Broccoli, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in broccoli (1/2 cup chopped, cooked)?
faqs.a: About 2.6 g, for 78 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.
No. Steaming, boiling, and roasting do not destroy fiber. They change texture and volume.
